learning_objective: Leerdoel 17: testresultaten en feedback analyseren om verbetermogelijkheden te identificeren
scope: Performance and shared action integration; no changes to real application data

method.queue: image-processing.json compares identical conversion work using sync vs database queue on the optimized code, not old vs new release. One warmup and five samples. Worker time is measured separately.
method.fixtures: Synthetic data only. Twenty, 200 and 1000 records; fixed description/comment sizes. Browser uses an isolated file database with 45 artworks and 50 comments.
method.controller: Two warmups and nine raw timed samples per dataset. Median, maximum, SQL count and JSON bytes retained. Controller and serialization only, excluding middleware, network, browser and images.
method.css: before-css.json was measured after a fresh production build immediately before changing CSS. Its CSS size matches before.json. after.json uses the new production build.

limitations: SQLite results do not establish MySQL production performance. Confirm EXPLAIN and concurrent load in staging.
No production TTFB, LCP or end-user device CPU benchmark was performed. No numeric browser CPU reduction is claimed.
Small comment collections incur pagination/response metadata overhead; all sizes are retained in comparison.json.
The number of homepage queries rises from 3 to 6, but all retrieved collections are bounded.
View-write comparison uses array cache; database-backed cache adds its own queries. Cache::has avoids repeated cache inserts; Redis is an optional deployment choice.
More image variants require storage and worker CPU. Queueing reduces request waiting, not total work. Synthetic compression ratios do not replace visual review of real art.
Admin production CSP already prevents Alpine execution. It was not weakened; browser.json retains all admin errors and stack traces. Admin CSS was checked separately using test-only bypassCSP.
Synthetic browser screenshots are functional evidence, not stakeholder approval of the design.
feedback: The requester explicitly approved all research priorities and emphasized using the existing Actions.
No visitor interviews or usability reviews have been invented; gather those before writing the stakeholder-feedback section of the portfolio.
findings_during_work: Cursor regression: formatting created_at before deriving the next cursor repeated pages. Generate cursors from database values before transforming response data. Regression test now passes.
Refresh test initially simulated new guest sessions. Persisting the session cookie verifies real same-visitor deduplication. First attempt retained.
Async conversion flags are updated by a worker on a different model instance. Unit assertions refresh media; the database-queue integration test verifies commit timing and original fallback.
Browser selectors initially ignored the author prefix inside comment paragraphs. The test was corrected and made self-resetting; first attempts are retained.
Existing SQLite rollback migration issue was encountered with DatabaseMigrations. Queue test uses normal RefreshDatabase transaction isolation; unrelated migrations were not changed.

Generated Filament assets were refreshed during verification. The public-site source does not load admin CSS. Real admin CSP still blocks Alpine; test-only bypass is explicitly labelled in browser.json and screenshots.
deployment: Run php artisan migrate to install feed indexes.
Build assets using pnpm run build.
Use QUEUE_CONNECTION=database (or a configured queue service); MEDIA_QUEUE=media separates conversion work.
Run a supervised worker: php artisan queue:work --queue=media,default --tries=3 --timeout=60 --memory=256 . Start with one media worker and measure capacity. Restart workers after deployment.
Keep worker timeout below the queue retry_after setting to avoid simultaneous duplicate execution; the recommended 60-second timeout fits the default 90-second database retry_after.
For legacy uploads, enqueue missing variants: php artisan media-library:regenerate --only=intro --only=card --only=display --only-missing . Existing originals remain the fallback.
Legacy media without saved dimensions still uses generated card/display URLs safely but omits srcset until metadata is available. Remote URL-only artworks retain their existing source.
reproduce: For a historical baseline, copy the same probe into a checkout of baseline_commit with dependencies installed; use a fresh build when comparing assets. Do not mix dev/HMR and production build measurements.

Install Playwright outside the repository, set PERFORMANCE_PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE to its index.mjs file URL and PERFORMANCE_BROWSER_CHANNEL to the installed Chrome/Edge channel, then run node scripts/performance/browser-check.mjs. It resets only the isolated fixture.
